candidate.answerReason: Pete and Claire are currently 20 and 8. Four years from now their ages will be 24 and 12, giving the required ratio.

methods.label: Start four years ago
methods.explanation:
Start at the earlier time so that both later ages can be expressed by adding the same number of years. Let \(c>0\) be Claire's age four years ago. Pete was then \(4c\).

Two years later, their ages were \(c+2\) and \(4c+2\), and Pete was three times Claire's age. Thus
\[
4c+2=3(c+2)=3c+6,
\]
so \(c=4\). Their current ages are therefore \(8\) and \(20\), respectively.

Let \(t\geq 0\) be the number of years from now until Pete is twice Claire's age. Then
\[
20+t=2(8+t)=16+2t,
\]
which gives \(t=4\). At that time they will be \(24\) and \(12\), so the answer is \(\boxed{4}\) years, choice \(\text{B}\).
